html:
The northern half of Korea, above the 38th parallel, under Soviet military rule from August 1945 to 1948. The map shows it in 1945.

When Japan collapsed in August 1945, Soviet troops entered Korea from Manchuria. The United States proposed splitting the country at the 38th parallel to take the Japanese surrender, and the Americans took the south. Meant to be temporary, the line became the division of Korea.

The Soviet command worked through local committees and promoted Kim Il Sung, a guerrilla leader who had fought Japan in Manchuria. Under its guidance land was taken from landlords and given to peasants in 1946, and industry was nationalised. Plans for one Korean government failed as the Cold War began. The Democratic People's Republic of Korea was declared in Pyongyang on 9 September 1948, and Soviet troops left at the end of that year. In 1950 Kim invaded the south, starting the Korean War. The two states are on the chart as North and South Korea.
